PullRequest.Title: github: add shared-process hosting and anonymous-read IPC
PullRequest.Body:
Related: microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#9678

- Register `GitHubService` in the shared process with shared-process identification, telemetry configuration and process-owned disposal.
- Add a separate typed, opt-in `ISharedProcessGitHubService` boundary for anonymous, API-relative JSON GET requests.
- Preserve cancellation/disconnect cleanup, shared engine admission/cooldowns, serializable response metadata and typed error details.
- Register the IPC client in desktop workbench and Agents entry points without migrating any existing caller.
- Add focused service/IPC regression coverage and document the preparation boundary.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: The shared process synchronously imports and constructs SharedProcessGitHubService during initServices, before InstantiationService is returned and channels/contributions initialize. Renderer entry points only register a delayed remote-service descriptor. The shared-process constructor allocates bounded maps/queue/telemetry/rate-limit state and a configuration listener; it performs no fetch, filesystem, IPC, or timer operation, so the added work is small fixed CPU/allocation on startup.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One engine and one channel per shared-process lifetime, plus one delayed renderer-side service descriptor per desktop window; cost does not scale with repositories, requests, or history while unused.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Startup construction is synchronous and single-instance. Existing configuration/storage initialization completes before this added construction; the diff adds no concurrent boundary work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No request cache is populated at startup. The engine's transport/cache is not created until an anonymous client is acquired, and telemetry schedules no timer until a request is recorded.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the startup reachability and bounded setup from SharedProcessMain.initServices, GitHubService's constructor, and the explicit no-fetch test.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact module-evaluation and allocation time is unmeasured, but the traced constructor performs only bounded in-memory setup and no heavyweight boundary operation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: although the setup is unconditional, the concrete work is fixed and lightweight rather than a realistic user-visible startup regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opt-in anonymous GitHub JSON read from a desktop window
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A caller awaits renderer-to-shared-process IPC, queue admission/cooldown, one shared-process fetch, bounded body read/JSON parsing, and response serialization back over IPC. This entire path is opt-in and search confirms no production ISharedProcessGitHubService caller in this PR or repository; existing workbench and Sessions callers remain on their prior engines.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serializes one request to the shared process and one GitHubRestResponse or typed error back to the caller.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One IPC call and one response per explicit getAnonymous invocation; no loop or collection fan-out is introduced.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This shared-process boundary did not exist; no existing caller is migrated, so current workflows retain their previous process-local behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both IPC legs are on the explicit caller's critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Performs an anonymous HTTPS GET and reads/parses a response bounded by the transport's 16 MiB maximum.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one fetch per distinct admitted in-flight coalescing key; up to 64 overlapping waiters can share it. Distinct requests are bounded by queue admission and concurrency.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The network operation is new only for consumers that opt into this new API; the PR migrates no existing production consumer or network request onto it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The fetch and JSON body processing are on the explicit caller's critical path after queue/cooldown delay.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Explicit call count and number of distinct URL/options coalescing keys. Identical overlapping reads share one operation; distinct retained requests are capped at 256, with 4 globally active, 2 per host/caller, and anonymous account serialization further limiting a single origin.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: RequestQueue caps global activity at 4 and host/caller activity at 2, while account-key exclusion serializes requests for the same anonymous origin. Identical reads coalesce with at most 64 waiters; there is backpressure rather than an unbounded burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Overlapping identical reads coalesce. The transport has an LRU/ETag cache while its anonymous client lease lives, but the IPC channel acquires and releases the lease per call, so sequential non-overlapping IPC calls reacquire a cold client; rate-limit cooldown state remains engine-owned. There is no negative cache. Because there are currently no production callers, this does not regress an existing workflow.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the only service references, request tests, queue limits, response-size cap, and transport coalescing implementation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Future caller frequency and response sizes are unknown. The mechanism and limits are established, but there is no current product scenario exercising this boundary.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the new boundary is unused by production code in this PR, and when explicitly used its network, serialization, concurrency, cancellation, and response allocation are bounded.

Scenarios.Scenario: Two windows issue the same anonymous read and one disconnects
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each window sends an IPC request; both acquire leases for the same normalized API base and attach to one coalesced transport operation. A disconnected/cancelled waiter detaches and releases its lease, while the network operation remains live for the peer; the last waiter cancellation aborts the fetch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Carries each window's request/cancellation and response independently.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two IPC calls for two callers; cancellation affects only one waiter.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: There was no cross-window shared-process read path; existing per-window engines could not share this operation across windows.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The surviving caller remains blocked only on the shared network operation, not on the disconnected peer.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Coalesces equivalent in-flight GETs into one fetch and aborts only after all waiters detach.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One fetch for the effective single coalescing key, not one per window.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing independent window engines would perform separate network operations; no existing caller is migrated in this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: One network response serves the surviving window; disconnect cleanup does not trigger a duplicate request.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of overlapping windows/waiters for one equivalent request, capped at 64 shared waiters.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One underlying operation for the coalescing key; cancellation is per waiter, and the final detached waiter aborts the operation. Global queue limits still apply across distinct keys.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: This is warm only at the in-flight coalescing level; completed sequential calls do not retain the per-client transport cache after the final lease is released. Cooldowns survive client release.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the IPC disconnect test, anonymous-client coalescing test, reference-counted lease implementation, and transport waiter cleanup.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No current production callers exercise cross-window sharing, so prevalence is zero in the reviewed revision and future multiplicity is unknown.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the introduced behavior reduces rather than amplifies overlapping network work and has bounded cleanup/lifetime.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 11 changed files and traced startup, IPC, network, serialization, cache, concurrency, cancellation, and disposal paths. No high-confidence, diff-introduced performance regression is present, and the PR does not itself fix a proven shipped performance regression.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
